answer: Each reef caps at eight members and the n-th joiner pays $25 times n squared. A new reef needs a $2,000 basalt anchor locked 90 days plus three endorsements. Five reef auditors rotate weekly and check admission logs within 48 hours. A comet sweep crosses reefs at random each epoch. A reef caught holding fakes loses its anchors and every member drops to zero weight for ten epochs. One hundred clones in one reef pay $8,458,750 in fees, or $67,500 spread over twenty reefs, against $2,500 for one hundred honest agents. A reef is a coral wall, and the comet sweep strips paint off fake shells.
